# s5i5 — mechanics learned, and where level 2 defeated me

Result: levels 0 and 1 solved (27 and 41 actions); level 2 not solved.

## The game

* Only action 6 (click) is ever legal.  Row 63 is a cosmetic step meter:
  after n actions of a level, round_half_up(64*n/BUDGET) cells at its right
  end turn 4.  BUDGET = 50 (lvl 0), 150 (lvl 1), 200 (lvl 2).
* The board holds **objects**: a solid rectangle of one colour with a 3-cell
  line of colour 3 glued to one edge (its tail) — the object grows AWAY from
  its tail.  Some objects carry a head cell (colour 13).
* Lineless objects are scenery: colour 15 never moves at all; other lineless
  bars (e.g. colour 1) can be shoved but never pass a shove on.
* At the bottom sits one control box per controllable colour: a 2-border
  panel showing a shape, a 3-coloured axis and the shape's mirror image.
  - clicking a pixel in the **far** (mirror) half grows that object by one
    3x3 block at its leading edge;
  - clicking the **near** half retracts the last block again (head moves
    back).  A retract on an object that has never grown is a no-op, and a
    non-head object refused to retract even after growing (lvl 2, c).
  - clicking anything else (borders, axis, board cells, heads, diamonds) is
    an inert but costed no-op.
* Target diamonds are 4 cells of colour 13 around an empty centre.  They are
  painted on top of whatever passes under them and never move.  A level is
  completed when **every** diamond centre holds a head (level 0 only
  advanced once the *second* head arrived).

## Pushing (the subtle part)

A growth whose new 3x3 block is occupied shoves what is there by 3 in the
same direction:

* the shoved object drags along everything touching it PERPENDICULAR to the
  push (transitively);
* an object dragged that way may in turn shove what is in front of it, but
  the *directly* shoved object may not — lvl 2 #84/#85 both failed exactly
  there, while lvl 1 #44 (c → a → b → e) succeeded;
* scenery is dragged like anything else but never passes a drag on, which is
  why 7 could not shove bar A down onto the 8-pillar (lvl 2 #71);
* anything blocked (grid edge, colour 15, an unmovable neighbour) makes the
  whole click a no-op, and the action still costs a step.
